AGENTS.md

scooter is an R package (roxygen2 + testthat, not on CRAN). It loads, preprocesses, and plots single-cell RNA-seq data on top of Seurat 5 and 6. inst/extdata/scrna-scooter.R is a docopt CLI that runs the package as a pipeline.

Roxygen documents each function. Read the function or man/<fn>.Rd first. This file covers only rules and traps that the code does not show.

Rules

  • Do not make git commits or write to git history. Leave changes in the working tree.
  • NAMESPACE and man/ are generated. Run Rscript -e 'roxygen2::roxygenise()'. Do not edit them.
  • Run air format . on the whole package after edits.
  • Use usethis helpers when one fits (use_package(), use_test()).
  • Loose .png, .pdf, and .log files in the repo root are generated output. Delete them.
  • End each response with a list of the files that changed. If you installed the package, give the install path.
Rscript -e 'testthat::test_local()'
Rscript -e 'pkgload::load_all("."); testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test-import.R")'
R CMD build . && R CMD check scooter_*.tar.gz

Writing style

These rules apply to all prose: roxygen, # comments, this file, and your responses.

  • Write about 80% of the way toward ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English.
  • Use direct language and short sentences. Put one main idea in each sentence.
  • Prefer familiar words when they preserve the meaning.
  • Remove repetition and unnecessary introductory phrases.
  • Preserve important technical details, assumptions, conditions, exceptions, and uncertainty.
  • Do not remove information only to make the answer shorter.
  • Prioritize clarity and accuracy over strict compliance with the standard.
  • Use the domain words that the code already uses. Do not invent abstractions or labels for them.
  • Function, package, and Seurat names stay as they are.
  • Keep # comments to one line unless the code is not clear without more.
  • A @param entry says what the parameter is, in one sentence. Do not add history or caveats that a caller does not need.

Seurat 5 and 6

  • Do not access assay slots. Use GetAssayData()/SetAssayData() with layer=.
  • On split layers, GetAssayData() stops with an error. LayerData() only warns and returns the first layer, so it silently drops the other samples. Use LayerData() only after JoinLayers().
  • merge() leaves layers split (counts.1, counts.2, …). Call SeuratObject::JoinLayers() after each merge.
  • Make reductions with CreateDimReducObject(), not new("DimReduc", ...).
  • VariableFeatures<- with NULL does nothing on Assay5. To clear the variable features, use DietSeurat().

Package vs. CLI

  • A package function wraps a Seurat function with the lab’s settings, plus the extra steps and plots of that step. Do not add a wrapper that only forwards arguments.
  • The CLI only sequences package functions, parses arguments, and writes the logs. It is also a staging area for unfinished functions. These move into the package later.
  • If a CLI function has the same name as a package export, move its extra behavior into the package function. Then delete the CLI copy. Do not rename the CLI copy.
  • Functions still to move: add_adt_assay_qc() (the only ADT CLR normalization), split_seurat_object() (target R/split.R), plot_adt_qc(), split_adt_hto_assay(), plot_hto_qc().

Code conventions

  • Verbs that touch expression data use S3: .default works on a plain matrix, and .Seurat extracts the data, calls .default, and puts the result back. Do not add this dispatch if the Seurat function already has it (check methods()).
  • In dr.R, the .Seurat methods call the Seurat functions directly. Always pass assay explicitly. Do not rely on DefaultAssay().
  • Each .Seurat method writes its plots to the working directory every time. There is no parameter to turn this off. tests/testthat/teardown.R deletes the files after the tests.
  • Names: read_* reads from disk, initialize_* builds a raw object, create_* returns a usable object. Write object in function names and obj in variable names.
  • Do not rename the file seurat_obj.qs2. Existing analysis dirs use it.
  • Name a single-object first parameter x.
  • Do not split one operation into two functions only because the input type differs.
  • Add a parameter only if the function body uses it.
  • Cell IDs are sample_name:barcode, with the Cell Ranger -1 removed.
  • Keep log_file = NULL and log with write_message(), one fact per call. Use message() for separator banners.
  • Get colors from get_color_scheme().
  • In new code, prefer intermediate variables to |> chains.
  • Add a shim to R/deprecated.R only if the old name was in a commit (git status shows M, not ??).

Traps

  • The CLI create step calls create_seurat_object() directly, not through do.call(). A top-level do.call() breaks LogSeuratCommand(), and normalize_counts() then fails.
  • The Sys.sleep(1) calls between plot writes keep the file times in order. Do not remove them.
  • mad_outlier_bounds() uses all cells on purpose, to match scater::isOutlier(). Do not add a debris pre-filter.
  • Per-sample splits use up to 30 dimensions. Merged and pooled analyses use up to 50. Keep both.
